subject: Usage pricing: baseline guarantee & surge credit structure
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tim Reynolds <tim.reynolds@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Usage pricing: baseline guarantee & surge credit structure

Hi Tim / Priya,

Great to meet yesterday — appreciate the deep dive into BrightPath's summarization use cases. Attaching a one-pager that outlines our hosted-API pricing levers (commit tiers, per-token rates, and burst behavior).

Quick notes to start the pricing conversation:
- We typically structure a monthly baseline guarantee (commit) and then an on-demand overage rate for tokens consumed above that commit.
- We offer surge credits when usage exceeds a short-term burst threshold (usually >120% of committed for a billing window) which can reduce incremental overage.
- We can cap bursts for predictability or allow uncapped bursts with a higher overage multiplier.

To get concrete: if you can share a target baseline monthly spend range (ballpark), I can run a tailored scenario for commit sizes, overage multipliers, and expected unit economics.

Questions for you:
1) Do you need a hard daily or monthly cap on bursts, or is predictable dollar exposure more important than absolute throttling?
2) Any procurement constraints for minimum monthly commitments or specific invoicing cadence?
3) Is there a compliance requirement (e.g., audit log retention) that should be in the contract?

I'll loop in Ben and Marissa (cc'd) to help model the numbers.

Attachments: RDW-pricing-1-pager.pdf

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Tim Reynolds <tim.reynolds@brightpathhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Usage pricing: baseline guarantee & surge credit structure

Dylan,

Thanks for the note and the one-pager. Couple of things from procurement and product:

- Procurement: our finance team prefers a monthly minimum floor vs. an annual lock. For early-stage usage we usually aim for a $30k–$50k/month floor. Can you confirm Redwood has a path for a monthly committed minimum?
- Product: we expect occasional spikes during quarterly reporting (short windows of heavy summarization) — ideally the burst should be allowed but with predictable economics.
- Overage: procurement asked for an on-demand over-commit multiplier cap — they proposed "on-demand = 2.5x per-token rate" for anything above the committed baseline.

We attached our procurement guidelines for your legal team. Also need to confirm: do you bill tokens per generated token or per prompt+completion combined? That affects our forecasting.

If you can sketch two scenarios (conservative: $30k/mo baseline; aggressive: $50k/mo baseline) with on-demand at 2.5x and an alternative at 1.9x, that would be helpful.

Best,
Tim Reynolds
Head of Product, BrightPath Health
Tim.Reynolds@brightpathhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Usage pricing: baseline guarantee & surge credit structure

Dylan / Marissa — looping in with a couple practical options we can present to BrightPath. I ran a quick model and added notes inline.

(quote) On Mon, Jan 18, 2027 at 11:02 AM Tim Reynolds <tim.reynolds@brightpathhealth.com> wrote:
> Procurement: our finance team prefers a monthly minimum floor vs. an annual lock. For early-stage usage we usually aim for a $30k–$50k/month floor. Can you confirm Redwood has a path for a monthly committed minimum?

Yes — we can do monthly committed tiers (month-to-month with a 30-day cancellation after term) or an annual commit with a smoother rate. For sales math: monthly commit gives BrightPath flexibility but we price slightly higher than annual to reflect churn risk.

Suggested scenarios to present (hosted API per-token costs shown as illustrative):
- Scenario A (Conservative): $30k/mo baseline (month-to-month). Base per-token rate = $0.0008. On-demand over-commit multiplier = 2.0x (i.e., $0.0016/token). Surge credit: apply 30% credit to tokens consumed between 120%–140% of baseline in a billing cycle (net effective multiplier 1.4x for that bucket).
- Scenario B (Aggressive): $50k/mo baseline (6-month commitment). Base per-token rate = $0.00065. On-demand over-commit multiplier = 1.8x (i.e., $0.00117/token). Surge credit: after 120% usage, first 20% of overage gets a 20% credit.

Operational options:
- Hard cap: enforce a hard daily burst cap to prevent runaway costs (we can surface alerts and automatically throttle at X% over baseline).
- Soft cap + alerts: allow uncapped bursts but auto-apply surge-credit buckets and give cost alerts at 100/110/120% thresholds.

Notes for legal/procurement:
- We typically define "baseline usage" in tokens/month with a definition for measurement (generated tokens + model context).
- Audit log/Aggregate usage reporting can be provided with 90-day retention by default; extended retention is an add-on.

I'll prepare a short spreadsheet with math once Dylan confirms which two scenarios to send to the customer.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tim Reynolds <tim.reynolds@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightpathhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Usage pricing: baseline guarantee & surge credit structure

Tim / Priya — appreciate the quick feedback. Based on Ben's modeling, here's a proposal we can put on the table (leaning toward predictability while preserving flexibility for your spikes):

Proposal (formalizing the two scenarios):
1) Month-to-month Pilot: $30,000/month baseline guarantee. Base rate = $0.0008/token. On-demand overage = 2.0x base rate. Surge credit: tokens from 120%–140% of baseline receive a 30% reduction to the overage rate (effective multiplier 1.4x applied only to that tranche). Hard daily cap can be set at BrightPath's request; default is uncapped.

2) 6-month Commitment: $50,000/month baseline guarantee. Base rate = $0.00065/token. On-demand overage = 1.8x base rate. Surge credit: first 20% over baseline gets a 20% credit to overage price. We recommend this for predictable unit economics during launch.

Other terms:
- Measurement: billing uses combined prompt + generated tokens. We provide daily usage exports and per-token breakdowns in the console.
- Audit logs: included at 90-day retention. Extended retention (12 months) available as an add-on; can add in SOW.
- DocuSign: I prepared a short contract and included a signing link below.

DocuSign (proposal): https://www.docusign.com/embedded/sign/abc123

Attachments: RDW-terms-docusign-link.txt

Next steps: if you prefer the 6-month option we'll draft the SOW and lock the rates; if you'd like to pilot, we can spin up the month-to-month and revisit at the 60-day mark. If either of you want a hard cap vs soft cap, tell me target dollar amount and Ben will propose throttle thresholds.

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Tim Reynolds <tim.reynolds@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Usage pricing: baseline guarantee & surge credit structure

Dylan — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what procurement expected. A couple quick asks before we sign:

1) Can you add a clause that guarantees a 5-business-day window for audit log retrieval requests? We need that for our SOC readiness review.
2) For the pilot (month-to-month), please enable soft caps with email alerts at 100/110/120% and an optional hard cap at $80k/mo if we hit an unexpected spike. We'll start with no hard cap but want the option turned on in the console.

We'll sign the pilot agreement today and include the SOW for extended retention as an add-on. Priya will handle the DocuSign — cc'd.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Tim
